title: PHP Patches Two Critical RCE Flaws That Were Already Under Attack
gist: PHP shipped emergency releases on October 21 for two CVSS 9.2 unauthenticated RCE flaws (php2shell) present since PHP 5.4; Amazon saw an exploitation attempt four days before patches, and a collapsed embargo, patch-lag across distros and an understaffed PHP security team dominated the response.

insights.claim: PHP 8.5.12, 8.4.27, 8.3.36 and 8.2.35 fix CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, both rated 9.2 under CVSS v4.0 and nicknamed php2shell; both are memory-safety failures in the request lifecycle that Sansec reports are present in every unpatched PHP since 5.4.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: A decade-plus installed base is exposed, making this a broad web-infrastructure risk event.
insights.quote: There are no complete mitigations; updating is the only safe choice.

insights.claim: Confirmed RCE exists for both bugs on Apache mod_php with default settings, PHP-FPM was validated only for the session lifecycle case, and FrankenPHP is considered likely susceptible from source analysis alone.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Real exposure depends on the SAPI, so triage should be by deployment model, not just PHP version.
insights.quote: no complete FPM exploit has been demonstrated for this SAPI
insights.locator: Exposure varies by how PHP is served

insights.claim: Severity is contested: both CVEs carry high attack complexity and additional attack requirements, and Sansec revised its expectation of mass exploitation after finding public exploits do not work against default PHP installs.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Mass exploitation risk may be lower than the headline suggests, though targeted attacks remain plausible.
insights.quote: The public exploits do not work against a default PHP installation.
insights.locator: How bad it proved is still contested

insights.claim: Many GitHub proof-of-concept repos for the flaws do not work on vanilla PHP, and malicious fake PoCs are spreading, with JFrog documenting prank versions including one that changed the victim's wallpaper.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Defenders testing with public PoCs risk self-infection, a secondary attack vector during incidents.

insights.claim: A third issue, CVE-2026-115560, remains unpatched; PHP advises setting session.upload_progress.enabled=0 until the next bugfix release.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Operators still have an open exposure after patching the two headline bugs.

themes.theme: Exploitation before patch and failed embargo

insights.claim: Amazon Threat Intelligence found an exploitation attempt dating to October 17 in MadPot telemetry, four days before the patches, from an IP tied to a commercial anonymization network, while Cloudflare deployed WAF rules about nine hours before release.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Zero-day exploitation preceded disclosure, so patching alone did not cover the earliest window and edge vendors provided the first defense.
insights.quote: from at least starting on October 17th
insights.locator: Attackers arrived before the patch did

insights.claim: Coordinated disclosure collapsed: CVE identifiers circulated two days early, a researcher mistakenly published a PoC video, and Chainguard unilaterally broke the embargo by publishing built images containing the fix, letting attackers study the fix in binary form.
insights.speaker: PHP Foundation
insights.so_what: Embargo discipline across the supply chain, including downstream image vendors, is a weak point in open-source security.
insights.quote: any attacker could now study the fix in binary form while every other PHP user was still waiting for the release
insights.locator: The coordinated disclosure had already collapsed

insights.claim: Chainguard's published policy, updated a month before the incident, allows it to shorten disclosure timelines when a vulnerability is discovered to be under active exploitation.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Conflicting disclosure policies between upstream projects and distributors will keep producing similar clashes.

insights.claim: Some operators took sites offline rather than wait for patches; the Dutch national cyber security centre and the Dutch House of Representatives took their own sites down as a precaution, while Sansec told stores they did not need to.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Divergent responses show uncertainty about real risk and the availability cost of precaution.
insights.locator: The Dutch national cyber security centre

insights.claim: Containers hid PHP dependencies from many operators, who found PHP behind OPNsense, OpenMediaVault, Nextcloud and Coolify, making asset inventory the first hurdle.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Hidden language-runtime dependencies in bundled software make fast patch response structurally hard.
insights.quote: containers obfuscated this away from me
insights.locator: Working out whether PHP was running at all

insights.claim: Package availability lagged unevenly: Debian Trixie landed quickly while Ubuntu, Red Hat and the official Docker images trailed, and Ondřej Surý's Launchpad PPA buckled under load.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Distribution lag extends the exposure window beyond upstream release time.
insights.locator: Then came the wait for packages

insights.claim: Confirming a patch is tricky: distro builds backport fixes so version strings stay old (Ubuntu 24.04's fixed package still reports 8.3.6), the CLI is not the web server, and FPM/Apache workers keep the old engine in memory until restarted.
insights.speaker: SirRobinBlibs
insights.so_what: Teams that trust php -v without restarting workers may believe they are patched when they are not.
insights.quote: Check the full package version against your distro’s tracker, not php -v.

insights.claim: The PHP Foundation says security work still depends on a small group of foundation-funded developers and there are too few of them.
insights.speaker: PHP Foundation
insights.so_what: Critical open-source infrastructure remains underfunded relative to its footprint, a recurring systemic risk.
insights.quote: today there are too few of them
insights.locator: Commenters on r/PHP asked how many people

insights.claim: PHP 8.1 and older get nothing from the project, though minimal backports were published for 7.4, 8.0 and 8.1 and Ubuntu issued fixes as far back as 14.04 under ESM; PHP 8.2 reaches end of life on December 31, 2026.
insights.speaker: Steef-Jan Wiggers
insights.so_what: Legacy PHP estates face upgrade or paid-extended-support pressure, a tailwind for commercial support vendors.
insights.locator: The upgrade gap drew the thread’s highest-voted comment
